akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾: you say "مَلِكٌ بَيِّنُ المُلْكِ" ("a king of evident kingship"), with the mīm in ḍamma. And you say "مَالِكٌ بَيِّنُ المَلْكِ" ("an owner of evident ownership") and "الملْكِ", with fatḥa on the mīm and with kasra; and they claim that ḍamma on the mīm is a dialectal variant in this meaning.

akhfash:3-3.t: And His words ﴿إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ are a badal (substitute) for ﴿مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ [2].

akhfash:6-6.t: And His words ﴿مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ﴾: He means "from the evil of the whisperer, from the jinn and mankind" (مِنْ شَرِّ الوَسْوَاسِ مِنَ الجِنَّةِ والنَّاسِ). And "الجِنَّة" are the jinn.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ﴾: their Creator and Owner. They are singled out for mention in honour of them, and in keeping with seeking refuge from the evil of the one who whispers in their breasts,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَلِكِ النَّاسِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِلَهِ النَّاسِ﴾: two badals (substitutes), or two ṣifas (adjectives), or two ʿaṭf bayāns (explicative appositions). The muḍāf ilayhi (genitive noun) is made overt in both for additional clarity.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ﴾, that is, the devil — named by the act (al-ḥadath) because of how constantly he engages in it — ﴿الْخَنَّاسِ﴾, because he slinks back and withdraws from the heart whenever Allah is remembered,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ﴾: their hearts, when they are heedless of the remembrance of Allah,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ﴾: a clarification (bayān) of the whispering devil, that he is of jinn and of humans, like His words, Exalted is He, «شياطين الجن والإنس» ("devils of the jinn and of humans") [Translator's note: the wording in the muṣḥaf (al-Anʿām 6:112) is «شَيَاطِينَ الْإِنْسِ وَالْجِنِّ».] Or «من الجنة» is a clarification of him, and «الناس» is conjoined to «الوسواس». On either view it includes the evil of Labīd and his aforementioned daughters. The first [view] has been objected to on the grounds that people do not have people whispering in their breasts; only the jinn whisper in their breasts. It was answered that people also whisper, in a sense befitting them, outwardly; then their whispering reaches the heart and becomes fixed in it by the path that leads to that. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿أَعُوذُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِرَبِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿مَلِكِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from رب. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إِلهِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from رب. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿مِنْ شَرِّ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعوذ. ﴿الْوَسْواسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْخَنَّاسِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from الوسواس.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, an adjective (ṣifa) of الوسواس. ﴿يُوَسْوِسُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي صُدُورِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:6-6.t:
﴿مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of يوسوس. ﴿وَالنَّاسِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الجنة.
This book is completed with the help of Allah the Exalted, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْوَسْواسِ): a noun meaning waswasa (whispering), like al-zalzāl meaning al-zalzala (shaking). As for the maṣdar, it is wiswās with kasra, like zilzāl. What is meant by it is Satan, named by the maṣdar as though he were a whispering in himself, because it is his craft and occupation; what is meant is "the possessor of whispering". In al-Miṣbāḥ it is also applied to what passes through the heart of evil and to everything in which there is no good. In al-Mukhtār: the speech of the soul; it is said "his soul whispered (waswasat) to him, a waswasa and wiswās with kasra", and al-waswās with fatḥa is the noun.
(الْخَنَّاسِ): in al-Mukhtār: "khanasa ʿanhu: he drew back from him, of the pattern dakhala; and akhnasahu another [Translator's note: the source runs the words together as "غيرهأي"], i.e. he left him behind and went on from him; and al-khannās is Satan because he withdraws (yakhnis) when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is mentioned." In Asās al-Balāgha it says: "A man khanasa from among the people, khunūsan, when he drew back and hid; and I khannastuhu and akhnastuhu; and he pointed with four fingers and khanasa his thumb (folded it in); and from this is al-khannās. In the ḥadīth: 'Satan whispers to the servant, and when he mentions Allah, he withdraws (khanasa).' And in his nose is a khanas, which is a lowering of the bridge and a broadness of the tip. And cattle are khunus."

* I'rab:
«قل أعوذ برب الناس ملك الناس إله الناس» قل is an imperative verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; the clause أعوذ is the quoted speech; أعوذ is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; برب الناس is attached to أعوذ; and ملك الناس and إله الناس are two badals (substitutes), or two adjectives, or two ʿaṭf bayān (explicative appositions). The annexation is repeated in both for added clarity. al-Zamakhsharī said in al-Kashshāf: "If you say: why was it not enough to state the muḍāf ilayhi, namely الناس, once? I say: because ʿaṭf bayān is for clarification, so it is a place for stating the noun overtly rather than using a pronoun." (مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْواسِ الْخَنَّاسِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعوذ; الوسواس is muḍāf ilayhi and الخناس is an adjective. (الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ) الذي is a naʿt of وسواس. al-Zamakhsharī said in al-Kashshāf: "All three vowel-marks are possible for its position: the genitive as an adjective, and the nominative and accusative as an expression of vilification." يوسوس is an imperfect verb, and في صدور الناس is attached to يوسوس. (مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ) is an explanation of the one who whispers, so من is explicative (bayāniyya). It may also be of beginning (ibtidāʾiyya), attached to يوسوس, i.e. he whispers in their breasts from the side of the jinn and from the side of mankind.
It may also be partitive (tabʿīḍiyya), i.e. being among the jinn and mankind. In al-Khaṭīb: it was said that it is an explanation of "mankind" in whose breasts it is, for it has been said that Iblīs whispers in the breasts of the jinn as he whispers in the breasts of mankind.

* Benefits:
1- From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Two surahs have been sent down to me the like of which have not been sent down, and you will never recite two surahs more beloved or more pleasing to Allah than they," meaning the two surahs of refuge (al-Muʿawwidhatān). The two surahs of refuge are also called al-Miqshiqshatān (the two that cure).
2- All the reciters agreed in this surah on dropping the alif from ملك, unlike al-Fātiḥa, in which they differed, as has preceded.
3- It is related from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ retired to his bed each night, he would join his palms, blow into them, and recite "Say: He is Allah, the One", "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak" and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind"; then he would wipe with them as much of his body as he could, beginning with his head and face and the front of his body. He would do that three times.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ﴾.
Iblīs whispers in the breast of man, and when he remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, he slinks back (خنس).

farraa:6-6.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
«الناس» here applies to the jinn and to mankind [Translator's note: the source has «النسا», evidently for «الناس»], as in your saying: he whispers in the breasts of people — their jinn and their humans. One of the Arabs said, while narrating: a group of jinn came and stood, and it was said: Who are you? They said: people (أناس) of the jinn. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿أنّه اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنّ﴾, so He made «النفر» of the jinn as He made them of mankind; and He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وأَنَّهُ كان رِجالٌ من الإِنْسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍ من الجنّ﴾, so He used «الرجال» of both jinn and mankind. And Allah knows best.
[The Book of al-Maʿānī is complete, and that is from Allah alone, who has no partner; praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; and may Allah bless Muhammad and his family and grant them peace.] [This blessed copy is complete, by the praise of Allah, His help and His good granting of success; and may Allah bless the one after whom there is no prophet, Muhammad, and his family and companions, and grant them abundant, everlasting peace until the Day of Judgement; and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Amen.]

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The preposition «من شر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَعُوذُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (من الجنة والناس) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {يُوَسْوِسُ}.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (برب الناس): the origin of (الناس), according to Sībawayh, is «أناس», and the alif and lām are a substitute for the hamza. Ibn al-Anbārī said: (الناس) is a plural that has no singular from its own wording, on a par with «الإبل» (camels), «الخيل» (horses), «النعم» (livestock), «البقر» (cattle), «الغزاة» (raiders) and «القضاة» (judges): these plurals have no singulars from their own wordings. He said: «الإنسان» is not the singular of (الناس), and «القاضي» is not the singular of «القضاة». He said: the measure of (الناس) in terms of the verb [pattern] is «فعل», and its origin is «نسي», from «نسيت» (I forgot); the ʿayn was put after and the lām before, so in status it became «نيس», and the yāʾ became an alif because it was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa. He said: some grammarians said: the origin of (الناس) is «الأناس»; the hamza was lightened, and a nūn was substituted for the quiescent lām of definiteness and assimilated into the nūn after it, so it became a doubled nūn, as Allah said (لكنا هو الله ربي), meaning «لكن أنا». He said: al-Farrāʾ invalidates this answer, saying: we found the Arabs saying in its diminutive «نويس». Al-Farrāʾ said: had what they said been correct, the diminutive would be «أنيس» and «أنيس». [Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; presumably two different vocalisations were intended.]
His saying (ملك) and (إله): a badal (substitute) for (رب) or a naʿt (adjective) of it. His saying (من الجنة والناس): (الناس) is genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to (الوسواس), i.e. from the evil of the whisperer and of the people. It is not permissible to conjoin it to (الجنة), because people do not whisper in the breasts of people; only the jinn whisper. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «لا يوسوسون في صدور والناس», evidently corrupt; rendered according to its evident sense.] So since the meaning [otherwise] is impossible, you take it as conjoined to (الوسواس).
The book is complete, by the praise of Allah and His favour; and may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his family and companions and grant them peace.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت". The clause ﴿قل﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.
﴿أعوذ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا". The clause ﴿أعوذ﴾ is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿برب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; and رب is muḍāf.
﴿الناس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ملك﴾: badal (substitute) of رب, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or naʿt (adjective); and it is muḍāf.
﴿الناس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿إله﴾: badal (substitute) of رب, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or naʿt (adjective) of it; and it is muḍāf.
﴿الناس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿من شر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; and شر is muḍāf.
﴿الوسواس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿الخناس﴾: naʿt (adjective), genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿الذي﴾: genitive (majrūr) [Translator's note: so in the source; الذي is indeclinable (mabnī), so it is genitive in position only] as a naʿt (adjective) of الوسواس; or a badal (substitute) of it; or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), since it behaves like the non-derived nouns; or in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he is the one who whispers in the breasts of mankind"; or in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) for censure (ʿalā al-dhamm) by an omitted verb, i.e. "I censure the one who whispers in the breasts of mankind".
﴿يوسوس﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to the relative noun. The clause ﴿يوسوس﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿في صدور﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يوسوس﴾; and صدور is muḍāf.
﴿الناس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿من الجنة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿يوسوس﴾.
﴿والناس﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿الوسواس﴾, or to ﴿الجنة﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The original form, according to Sībawayh, is أناس, and the alif and lām [of الناس] are a replacement for the hamza.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: A naʿt (adjective). One says: ملك بيّن المُلك (a king with evident kingship), and مالك بيّن المِلك والمُلك (an owner with evident ownership and kingship).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْواسِ: it is the one who whispers into the breasts, as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Basīṭ] 600-
تسمع للحلي وسواسا إذا انصرفت ... كما استعان بريح عشرق زجل
(You hear a jingling (وسواس) from her ornaments when she turns away, like the rustling of the ʿishriq plant calling on the wind for help.)
الْخَنَّاسِ: from Ibn ʿAbbās there are two narrations. One of them is that he whispers and crouches upon a person's breast, and when Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is mentioned, he slinks back (يخنس). The other narration is that he whispers, and when he is obeyed he withdraws (انخنس). The two views agree.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: In the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a naʿt (adjective); and the nominative is permissible by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
One says: جنّيّ, جنّ and جنّة; the hāʾ is for the feminine of the collective, like حجار and حجارة. Abū Jaʿfar said: I asked ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, وَالنَّاسِ: how are they conjoined to الْجِنَّةِ when they do not whisper? He said: They are maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الوسواس, and the implied order is: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind from the evil of the whisperer and of mankind (من شرّ الوسواس والناس)." What he said is good, because placing earlier and later with the wāw is permissible, good and frequent, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 601-
جمعت وفحشا غيبة ونميمة ... ثلاث خصال لست عنها بمرعوي
(You have combined — along with obscenity — backbiting and talebearing: three traits from which you do not desist.)
And Ḥassān said «2»: [al-Ṭawīl] 602-
وما زال في الإسلام من آل هاشم ... دعائم غرّ ما ترام ومفخر
وهم جبل الإسلام والنّاس حولهم ... رضام إلى طود يروق ويقهر
بهاليل منهم جعفر وابن أمّه ... عليّ ومنهم أحمد المتخيّر
(There have never ceased to be in Islam, from the family of Hāshim, illustrious pillars that cannot be reached, and a source of pride; they are the mountain of Islam, and the people around them are boulders beside a lofty peak that excels and overpowers; noble chiefs: among them Jaʿfar and his mother's son ʿAlī, and among them Aḥmad the chosen one.)
So he began the wording with Jaʿfar, then brought ʿAlī after him, then brought the Prophet ﷺ after him, though he is the foremost in reality. «[Translator's note: «2» is a footnote marker in the source whose footnote text is not included here.]»

safi-cedvel:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(بربّ) is attached to (أعوذ). (ملك) is a badal of ربّ – or a naʿt or ʿaṭf bayān to it –, genitive. (إله) is a badal of ملك, genitive. (من شرّ) is attached to (أعوذ). (الذي) is a relative in the position of genitive, a naʿt of الوسواس. (في صدور) is attached to (يوسوس). (من الجنّة) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يوسوس..
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «أعوذ ... » is in the position of accusative, the thing said.
And the clause: «يوسوس ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).

* Morphology:
(الوسواس): a name for the one who whispers (yuwaswis); its wazn is فعلال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(الخنّاس): an intensive form of the active participle from the triliteral خنس, i.e. "withdrew and hid".

* Benefits:
1- Harmony of sound and meaning:
The subject of this sūra is seeking refuge with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from the whispering (waswasa) of Satan, and whispering is the subject of this sūra. Therefore the letter sīn is repeated in each of its verses and recurs in its words, so that, when reciting it, we hear a tune that translates whispering for us, and on hearing it we sense an atmosphere of whispering, even if we do not know its subject. Thus meaning and melody agree in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and support one another.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {مَلِكِ الناس إله الناس}: they may be two adjectives of «ربِّ الناسِ», or two badals (substitutes), or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «مَلِكِ الناسِ، إلهِ الناس» — what are they in relation to «ربُّ الناسِ»? I say: they are ʿaṭf bayān, as in your saying: 'the conduct of Abū Ḥafṣ, ʿUmar al-Fārūq'. It was clarified by «مَلِكِ الناس», then further clarification was added, because «رَبُّ الناسِ» may be said of another, as in His saying: {اتخذوا أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَاباً مِّن دُونِ الله} [al-Tawba: 31]; and 'king of mankind' may be said [of another]; but «إلهُ الناس» is exclusive, with no partnership in it, so it was made the utmost of clarification." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] objected that clarification (bayān) is by non-derived nouns (jawāmid). This is answered by saying that this is treated like non-derived nouns; its establishment was given at «الرحمن الرحيم» at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it said «برَبِّ الناسِ», in construct with them specifically? I say: because the seeking of refuge occurs from the evil of the whisperer in the breasts of people, so it is as though it were said: I seek refuge from the evil of the one who whispers to people, in their Lord who owns their affairs." Then he said: "If you say: why was it not sufficient to make the governed noun [«الناس»] overt once? I say: because it is ʿaṭf bayān, so it was a place calling for the overt [noun]." [Translator's note: the source wording here, «لأنَّ عطفَ البيانِ فكان», is defective; it is rendered according to its evident sense.]

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {الوسواس}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "A noun in the sense of al-waswasa (whispering), like al-zalzāl in the sense of al-zalzala; as for the maṣdar (verbal noun), it is wiswās with kasra, like al-zilzāl. What is meant by it is the devil, named by the maṣdar as though he were whispering itself, because it is his craft and occupation; or 'the possessor of whispering' is meant." — end of quote. Discussion with him has already passed on [the claim] that the form with kasra is the maṣdar and the form with fatḥa the noun, in al-Zalzala; let it be consulted.
His saying: {الخناس}: i.e. the one who keeps withdrawing, because when Allah the Exalted is mentioned he slinks back (khanasa). It is an intensive form from al-khunūs. The derivation of this root was given in Sūrat al-Takwīr.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {الذى يُوَسْوِسُ}: it may be in the genitive as a naʿt (adjective), a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), because it is treated like non-derived nouns (jawāmid); and it may be accusative or nominative by severance (qaṭʿ).

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {مِنَ الجنة}: there are several views on it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from «شَرِّ» with repetition of the governor, i.e. "from the evil of the jinn". The second: it is a badal from «ذي الوَسواس» [the one with whispering], because the whisperer is of the jinn and of mankind. The third: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُوَسْوِسُ», i.e. he whispers while being of these two kinds. The fourth: it is a badal from «الناس», with «مِنْ» made explicative (tabyīn); the name "people" (al-nās) was applied to the jinn because they move about in their aims — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. However, al-Zamakhsharī invalidated it, saying after relating it: "They cited as evidence {نَفَرٌ} [al-Jinn: 1] and {رِجَالٌ} [al-Jinn: 6]. How unworthy it is! For the jinn were called jinn because of their concealment (ijtinān), and people were called nās because of their being manifest, from al-īnās, which is seeing, just as they were called bashar. And even if al-nās applied to both kinds and that were sound and established, it would not be suited to the eloquence of the Qurʾān and its remoteness from artificiality. Better than that is for al-nās to be meant as al-nāsī (the forgetful), as in His saying: {يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الداع} [al-Qamar: 6], and as was read: {مِنْ حيث أفاضَ الناسي}; then it was clarified by «الجِنة» and «الناس», because the two weighty ones (al-thaqalān) are the two kinds characterised by forgetting the right of Allah the Exalted." I say: he means that the kasra sufficed in place of the yāʾ, and that what is meant is the active participle; the verification of this was given in al-Baqara, and I recited some attestations for it there.
The fifth: it is a clarification (bayān) of «الذي يوسوِسُ», on the basis that the devil is of two kinds, human and jinn, as He said: {شَيَاطِينَ الإنس والجن} [al-Anʿām: 112]; and it is related of Abū Dharr that he said to a man: "Have you sought refuge from the devils of mankind?" The sixth: it is attached to «يُوَسْوِس», with «مِنْ» marking the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), i.e. he whispers in their breasts from the direction of the jinn and from the direction of mankind. The seventh: «والناس» is conjoined to «الوَسْواس», i.e. "from the evil of the whisperer and of people". It cannot be conjoined to «الجِنة», because people do not whisper in the breasts of people; only the jinn whisper; so since the meaning is impossible, it was construed as conjoined to «الوَسْواس» — Makkī said this; it is very far-fetched because of the resulting ambiguity, and it was stated before that people also whisper, in a sense befitting them.
The eighth: {مِنَ الجنة} is a ḥāl from «الناس», i.e. being of the two kinds — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, but he did not make clear which of the preceding [occurrences of] «الناس» is the one to which the ḥāl belongs. On every supposition the circumstantial meaning is not sound [in any of them], neither the first nor what follows it. Then he said: "It was also said: it is conjoined to «الجِنة»", meaning the last «والناسِ» is conjoined to «الجِنة». This wording calls for something to have preceded it, namely that «الناس» be conjoined to something other than «الجِنة», as Makkī held, and then for him to say: "It was also said: it is conjoined to «الجِنة»". In sum, it is loosely worded speech — [may Allah overlook it for us] and for him and for all His creation, by His grace and generosity, and seal [our lives] for us with good from Him, and seal for us His good pleasure with us and with all the Muslims.
This is the last of what was made easy for me in dictating this subject and gathering what is in this compilation, seeking a means to Him through His speech and asking for the intercession before Him of His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, that He make it purely for His face and a cause of success with Him; for He is sufficient for me, and the best Disposer of affairs. Its completion, in composition and writing, coincided with the middle ten days of the month of Rajab the solitary, of the year seven hundred and thirty-four — may Allah make its passing good, by His grace and generosity. Said and written by the neediest of His servants towards Him, Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad [ibn] Masʿūd al-Shāfiʿī al-Ḥalabī, praising Allah, Lord of the worlds, and invoking blessings upon His trustworthy Messenger and his family and all his Companions, and peace.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ (١)).
We mentioned at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara that the origin of «نَاس» according to Sībawayh is «أُنَاس», its fāʾ [the first radical] having been dropped; according to others nothing was dropped from it, and its origin is «نَوْس», because they say in the diminutive «نُوَيْس».
Some said: its origin is «نَيْس», transposed from «نَسِيَ», taking it from «النِّسْيَان» (forgetting); but this is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ (٤) الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ (٥)).
(الْوَسْوَاسِ) with a fatḥa is a noun, and with a kasra it is the maṣdar (verbal noun); the implied form is: «مِنْ شَرِّ ذِي الْوَسْوَاسِ» (from the evil of the one who whispers). It is also said that Satan was named by the act itself, for intensification. (الْخَنَّاسِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of it. (الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ) may be nominative, accusative or genitive.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ): it is a badal (substitute) for «شَرِّ» with repetition of the governor (ʿāmil), i.e. «مِنْ شَرِّ الْجِنَّةِ» (from the evil of the jinn). It is also said that it is a badal for «ذِي الْوَسْوَاسِ», because the whisperer is of the jinn.
It is also said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُوَسْوِسُ», i.e. he whispers while being of the jinn.
It is also said that it is a badal for «النَّاسِ», i.e. in the breasts of the jinn;
and [the one who held this] made «مِنَ» explicative (tabyīn), and applied the name «النَّاس» to the jinn because they move about in pursuit of their aims.
«الْجِنّ» and «الْجِنَّة» have one meaning. It is also said that (مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ) is a ḥāl from «النَّاسِ», i.e. being of the two kinds. As for the last (النَّاسِ), it is said that it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «ذِي الْوَسْوَاسِ», i.e. from the evil of the two kinds.
It is also said that it is maʿṭūf to «الْجِنَّةِ».

zajjaj:4-4.t:
Sūrat al-Nās
Meccan
﷽
”الوَسْواسِ“ ("the whisperer") is Satan. One says ”وَسْوَسَ في صَدْرِهِ“ ("he whispered in his breast") and ”وَسْوَسَ إلَيْهِ“ ("he whispered to him"). ”اَلْوَسْوَسَةُ“ is hidden, confused speech, and ”اَلْوَسْواسُ“ is a noun from it. It has been explained here as meaning "from the evil of the one possessed of whisperings", that is, Satan; so ”اَلْوَسْواسُ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun). This pattern comes in reduplicated [roots], like ”زِلْزالٌ“, and it is rare in others, like ”تَحْنانٌ“.
﴿الخَنّاسِ﴾ ("the one who withdraws") is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) of ”خَنَسَ“, meaning "he shrank back and withdrew"; its maṣdar is ”خُنُوسٌ“, like ”جُلُوسٌ“. The whole root revolves around this basic sense: the receding stars (al-nujūm al-khunnas) are those that withdraw from their course and disappear in the light of the sun. In the ḥadīth: ”اَلشَّيْطانُ يُوَسْوِسُ إلى العَبْدِ، فَإذا ذَكَرَ اللَّهَ خَنَسَ“ ("Satan whispers to the servant, and when he remembers Allah, he withdraws"), that is, he shrinks back and withdraws. And ”اَلْخَنْسُ“ in the nose is its being set back from the head and raised above the lip. And ﴿الجِنَّةِ﴾ [al-Nās: 6] means the jinn; the word has occurred many times before. He mentioned the jinn and mankind in order to seek refuge from everything that whispers evil, whether it be from the devils or from human beings.
